questions.answer: The equation is \(z^2=-1\). Since \(i^2=-1\), the two roots are \(z=i\) and \(z=-i\).
Factor: \(z^2-4=(z-2)(z+2)\). Therefore \(z=2\) or \(z=-2\).
Move the constant: \(z^2=-9\). Since \(-9=9i^2\), \(z=\pm3i\).
The discriminant is \(\Delta=2^2-4(1)(2)=-4\). Hence \(z=(-2\pm i\sqrt4)/2=-1\pm i\).
Divide by \(3\) to get \(z^2-4z+5=0\). The discriminant is \(16-20=-4\), so \(z=(4\pm2i)/2=2\pm i\).
Factor by inspection: \(z^2+(2-2i)z-4i=(z+2)(z-2i)\). Hence \(z=-2\) or \(z=2i\).

questions.prompt: Explain why the roots of \(z^2-2z+10=0\) must be conjugates, then find them.
questions.answer: The coefficients are real, so non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs. The discriminant is \(4-40=-36\), giving \(z=(2\pm6i)/2=1\pm3i\), which are conjugates.

questions.prompt: Find a monic quadratic with real coefficients whose roots are \(2+i\) and \(2-i\).
Find \(p\) and \(q\) if \(z^2+pz+q=0\) has roots \(-1+4i\) and \(-1-4i\).
questions.answer: For a monic quadratic, the sum of roots is \(-p\) and the product is \(q\). The sum is \(-2\), so \(p=2\); the product is \((-1)^2+4^2=17\), so \(q=17\).

questions.prompt: For which real \(m\) does \(z^2+2z+m=0\) have a repeated complex root?
questions.answer: A repeated root occurs when \(\Delta=0\). Here \(\Delta=2^2-4m=4-4m\), so \(m=1\); the repeated root is \(z=-1\).

questions.prompt: For which real \(m\) does \(z^2+4z+m=0\) have two non-real roots?
questions.answer: With real coefficients, two non-real roots occur when \(\Delta<0\). Here \(\Delta=16-4m\), so \(16-4m<0\), hence \(m>4\).

questions.prompt: Find all real \(m\) such that \(z=1+i\) is a root of \(z^2+mz+2=0\).
A learner says \(z^2+2z+5=0\) has no roots because the discriminant is negative. Diagnose and solve correctly.
questions.answer: That conclusion is valid over real numbers only, not over \(\mathbb C\). Here \(\Delta=4-20=-16\), so \(z=(-2\pm4i)/2=-1\pm2i\).

questions.prompt: Show directly that if \(u+iv\) is a root of a real-coefficient quadratic, then \(u-iv\) is also a root.
questions.answer: Let \(p(z)=az^2+bz+c\) with real \(a,b,c\). Conjugating \(p(u+iv)=0\) gives \(a(u-iv)^2+b(u-iv)+c=0\), because conjugation preserves sums and products and fixes real coefficients. Thus \(u-iv\) is also a root.

questions.prompt: Use completing the square to solve \(z^2-2iz-2=0\).
questions.answer: Move the constant: \(z^2-2iz=2\). Add \((-i)^2=-1\) to both sides: \((z-i)^2=1\). Therefore \(z-i=\pm1\), so \(z=1+i\) or \(z=-1+i\).
